subject: Chain-of-custody for ephemeral logs & cross-border retention limits
messages:
From: Priya Desai <priya@acmehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on ephemeral node logs after last week's outage

Hi Logan / Karthik,

Thanks again for the rapid response during the incident on Tuesday. Our security team has a couple of follow-ups around retention and transfer of ephemeral diagnostic logs that were captured during the failover:

- What is Redwood's recommended retention window for ephemeral GPU node logs and KV cache slices related to a confirmed incident?
- If we need to transfer a subset of those logs to our internal forensics team in EU, what steps do you take to ensure chain-of-custody and compliance with cross-border data movement?

We're particularly sensitive because some session identifiers might map to EU resident accounts. Please advise what redaction or partitioning options exist and whether Redwood can produce an evidentiary export (signed manifest, checksums) that our auditors will accept.

Appreciate any quick guidance.

—Priya
Priya Desai
Director, Security & Compliance
Acme Health Systems
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral node logs after last week's outage

Priya — thanks for raising this. High-level answers up front, then I outline a short action plan we can follow with Acme's forensics team.

1) Retention window: For ephemeral node-level diagnostic logging (kernel dumps, per-request traces, KV cache slices) we typically retain a 21-day hot window for debugging and 90 days in cold archive for confirmed incidents. Shorter retention is possible for regulated customers via configuration (we can set a 30-day archive-only policy if needed).

2) Cross-border transfer & chain-of-custody: We can produce an evidentiary export bundle that includes: signed manifest, SHA256 checksums, TTLs, and MD5 where requested. Transfers use an encrypted transfer endpoint (S3 with customer-managed KMS or pre-signed one-time link) and are logged to an immutable audit trail. We also timestamp the export and include operator attestation.

3) Redaction/partitioning: Before export we can run a redaction pass to remove PII/session identifiers scoped to EU users, or we can slice the dataset to only include non-EU session fragments. This is a manual step triggered by an authorized request; it requires coordination with our infra team.

Action items I propose:
- Karthik: prepare a short export checklist and indicate which log buckets/how-to slice KV cache.
- Evelyn: confirm whether 90-day cold archive causes any compliance flags for Acme if we transfer EU-resident slices.
- Logan: prepare an evidentiary bundle template (manifest + checksums) and attach a retention matrix.

I'll attach the retention_matrix.xlsx and a chain_of_custody_template.pdf for your review. Happy to set a quick call if you want to walk through the export.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral node logs after last week's outage

Priya/Logan,

Quick technical note on the artifacts:
- Node diagnostic logs: stored in ephemeral VM disks for up to 7 days, then ingested into centralized logging (ELK) where retention policies apply. For incident exports we pull the original VM slices plus the centralized logs to preserve context.
- KV cache slices: these are not persisted by default beyond node lifetime; for incidents we snapshot the in-memory cache and write to an encrypted S3 bucket (expiring objects per the retention policy).
- Correlation: we can map request IDs to traces but we will not share full user payloads unless explicitly requested under an evidence request.

For cross-border exports we support two patterns:
A) Redacted bundle: redact user identifiers at export time and provide a manifest showing fields removed.
B) Escrowed export: we can transfer the bundle to your EU-based s3 endpoint (customer-managed) — we do not hold the exported copy beyond the agreed transfer window.

I'll prepare the export checklist (SEC-784) and drop it into the Jira ticket and the Drive link Logan shared. Marcus, please confirm ops capacity for a same-day export if Acme requests it.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Infra Reliability
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@acmehealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral node logs after last week's outage

Priya — quick legal/compliance check:
- 90-day cold archive is acceptable in general, but for EU-resident data we need explicit customer consent for cross-border transfer unless the dataset is redacted to remove personal data.
- If Acme requests raw exports containing EU identifiers, we must record the legal basis and log the export in our compliance ledger. That also triggers a PII handling checklist (encryption at rest with customer-managed keys recommended).

We can offer reduced retention (e.g., 30 days) and a redaction workflow to avoid cross-border movement. If Acme opts for transfer to their EU bucket, request must come from an authorized Acme admin and include an export justification.

I'll coordinate the PII checklist and sign-off matrix.

—Evelyn Hart
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral node logs after last week's outage

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps for Acme: 

1) Proposed default: 21-day hot retention + 90-day encrypted cold archive for incident artifacts. For Acme we can change the cold archive to 30 days if preferred (ops config).
2) Export options:
   - Redacted export (recommended for EU data): Redwood performs automated redaction of PII/session ids, produces a signed manifest and checksums, and uploads to Acme's EU S3 endpoint.
   - Direct escrow: Redwood snapshots raw artifacts and transfers to Acme's secure bucket; Redwood will not retain the transferred copy beyond the agreed transfer window.
3) Required approvals: an authorized Acme admin must submit an export request form (see linked Jira SEC-784) and indicate whether redaction is required.
4) Timeline & attachments: If Acme submits the form today, we can produce a redacted evidentiary bundle within 24 hours. Attached are the retention_matrix.xlsx and chain_of_custody_template.pdf for your legal team.

Would you like me to schedule a 30-minute handoff call with our ops and compliance teams, Priya?

Best,
Logan Wright
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
